nodes.label: A7 · Onboarding-transfer (leave-one-venue-out)
nodes.rationale: Forecast = donor DOW shape x own level over a 14-day cold-start window used only to anchor the held-out venue's level; baseline is per-venue seasonal-naive on the same window so each per-venue comparison shares a denominator and is scale-fair.

nodes.label: LOVO harness — per-fold 7-day blocks with MCS + paired moving-block bootstrap
nodes.rationale: Scoring on consecutive 7-day blocks makes the comparison carry dispersion — a 90% MCS and a paired moving-block bootstrap CI on transfer minus naive, rather than a bare win count (ledger M23).

nodes.label: G2 — venues do not share a ruler
nodes.rationale: Ellel admits no defensible scaled error, so it is scored on unscaled MAE in pounds and reported on its own; the loss column names each row's unit and rows in different units are not comparable. The earlier three-venue pool averaged pounds-denominated blocks with dimensionless MASE series, so its null was reached by an inadmissible route even though the direction was unchanged.

nodes.label: calendar_lag7_active basis correction — both scaled rows now exceed MASE 1
nodes.rationale: On the basis the estate ruled, transfer scores 1.242 at the Beer Hall against 0.872 on the calendar_lag7 basis this module used to hard-code. Above one is worse than the seasonal-naive reference the denominator is built from, so beating the cold-window baseline is a statement about that baseline being poorer still, not about transfer being good. The denominator changed; the forecasts did not.

nodes.label: Withdrawn estate-level claim — a count over two venues carries no majority
nodes.rationale: Only 2 of 3 venues can enter a scaled comparison and one (Two River Taps) was closing at measurement, so the gate's original >=2-of-3 criterion is not evaluable. The per-venue rows stand individually; the estate-level claim is withdrawn on the grounds that the evidence base was never admissible, not weakened.

nodes.label: Crossover sweep — transfer wins fall away as history accrues
nodes.rationale: Built to tell a partial-pooling story (transfer wins while the venue is data-poor, then hands over to its own seasonal-naive). The shape is still consistent with it, but at every window the denominator is 2, so the descent is a sequence of counts out of two and is equally consistent with one venue's behaviour plus noise. Reported as a description of two venues, not evidence for a cold-start regime.

nodes.label: Foundation-model rung — zero-shot chronos adopted over the global GBM
nodes.rationale: Rolling origin, 24 folds at horizon 7, paired within fold, zero dropped. Beer Hall 0.643 vs 0.760, Two River Taps 0.595 vs 0.811, both CIs excluding zero. Scored only where a scaled error is defensible (G2) and adoption requires a win at EVERY such venue, so one venue cannot carry the rung.

nodes.label: In-context fine-tuning — forward note
nodes.rationale: The hand-built shape-transfer is the analogue of conditioning a held-out venue on the donor's shape; a foundation backbone with in-context fine-tuning would condition on the donor series directly, and the LOVO harness is exactly the test it must pass to be adopted.

nodes.label: Two-clause A7 gate (transfer NOT EVALUABLE, foundation PASS)
nodes.rationale: The two clauses are reported separately so neither can carry the other: the transfer clause needs a majority over three scaled venues and the estate supplies two, so it is NOT EVALUABLE; the foundation clause PASSES and is adopted. Overall verdict is governed by the transfer clause.

nodes.label: Runtime identity stamp (.venv-forecast, Python 3.12.13, mps, store ceiling)
nodes.rationale: Environment, compute device, pinned library versions and the store ceiling (2026-07-07) are stamped on the result so a reported number is attributable to an exact runtime and can be reproduced or invalidated.
